newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close firmer as U.S. treasuries rally.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close firmer as U.S. treasuries rally.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed firmer in light trading on Wednesday after a stronger Canadian dollar and a mini-rally in U.S. treasuries boosted market confidence, analysts said.

"It's been a reasonably quiet day with longer ends performing a little bit better," said Mark Chandler, senior economist with Goldman Sachs Canada. "Some of it is definitely currency-related because we opened up about 70 basis points better than where we closed yesterday."
The Canada dollar closed slightly weaker at C$1.3737 (US$0.7279) on Wednesday from an open of C$1.3722 (US$0.7288).

"There are rumors of the usual suspects, the futures exchanges and people like that, buying Canada (dollars)...and that is fairly supportive for the bonds as well," said Jim Webber, vice-president and director of fixed-income research with Toronto Dominion Securities Inc.
Canada's benchmark 30-year long bond rose C$0.27 to C$118.54 to yield 6.574 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond enjoyed a 10/32 gain to yield 6.56 percent.
The spread between the two benchmark bonds moved to a spread of one basis point, the same as on Tuesday.
Canadian bonds have rallied since the U.S. Federal Reserve decided not to raise interest rates at its Federal Open Market Committe meeting on July 2.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond jumped C$0.31 to C$109.47 to yield 5.959 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent, which gained 4/32 to yield 6.25 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds widened to 29 basis points from 25 basis points at the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.09 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.10 percent.
